prompt: Before you touch a single byte of MERIDIAN data you must prove your workstation is configured to the task force standard. Which keyboard shortcut opens the global Settings window in Inseyets.PA?
validationMethod: Tools > Settings, or Ctrl+T.

prompt: The task force SOP requires that your configuration apply to every device you open today, not just the first one. Settings made under the Tools menu apply to:
options: Only the project that is currently open
All open and future projects after the configuration change
Only projects created after Inseyets.PA is restarted
Only the extraction highlighted in the Project Tree
acceptedAnswers: All open and future projects after the configuration change
validationMethod: Tools settings are global; Project Settings (Ctrl+P) are per-project.

prompt: Your collection order requires cryptographic verification of every image. Which hash algorithms does Inseyets.PA use to verify extractions? (Select all that apply.)
validationMethod: Inseyets.PA uses SHA256 and MD5; one or both may be used to verify extractions.

prompt: The cell chief wants every analyst on IRON MERIDIAN running an identical build. You export your configuration so it can be pushed to the rest of the team. What file extension does an exported Inseyets.PA settings configuration file use? (Include the dot.)
validationMethod: Tools > Settings > Export saves an Inseyets.PA Settings Configuration file (*.cnf).

prompt: Task force reporting policy states that no product may leave the cell without a mission number recorded. You add a custom report field named 'Mission Number' at Tools > Settings > Additional Report Fields. What must you set on that field so a report CANNOT be generated until the field is filled in?
validationMethod: Additional Report Fields > Add New > set Required = Yes.

prompt: ALPHA was seized in the Eastern Time zone and the targeting board briefs in local time. You set the project time zone to (UTC-05:00) New_York (America). What effect does this setting have on the extraction itself?
options: It rewrites the timestamps stored inside the extraction files
It only affects how timestamps appear in Inseyets.PA; it does not alter data in the extraction
It permanently converts all timestamps to UTC +0
It deletes and re-parses the extraction using the new zone
acceptedAnswers: It only affects how timestamps appear in Inseyets.PA; it does not alter data in the extraction
validationMethod: Project Settings (Ctrl+P) > Time zone settings (UTC). Display only.

prompt: The collection team sent you two files alongside the ALPHA extraction folders. Which file type points to MULTIPLE extractions of the same device, contains the hash and HMAC string, and can be opened in any text editor?
validationMethod: A single extraction creates a .ufd; multiple contiguous extractions create a .ufdx containing the hash and HMAC string.

prompt: Enrichment engines cost processing time, so the cell applies most of them after ingest. Which single enrichment engine MUST be run during initial processing because it depends on raw file metadata and cannot be applied later?
validationMethod: All other enrichment engines can be applied after initial processing and opening.

prompt: Build case ALPHA with BOTH provided extractions loaded (File System first, then add the Advanced Logical through Edit case > Add evidence > Load extraction). How many extractions are listed in the Extraction Summary area when you are finished?
validationMethod: Close the case, three-dot menu > Edit case, add the second extraction; both appear in Extraction Summary.

prompt: Open the Extraction Summary for ALPHA and select Data Details View. What is the END date and time recorded for the Advanced Logical extraction?
validationMethod: Extraction Summary > Data Details View shows extraction start/end time and date, device model and name, and extraction type. Instructor: record the observed value.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Individual extractions are colour coded in the Project Tree so you can tell at a glance which extraction a record came from. What colour is assigned to the extraction named File System in your ALPHA project?
validationMethod: Colour codes are set at Tools > Settings > Models. Instructor: record the observed colour.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: You want to change the colour Inseyets.PA assigns to a device data type so ALPHA and BRAVO are visually distinct in merged views. Where do you change it?
validationMethod: Models settings customise colour schemes for device data types.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: The MERIDIAN network is known to use throwaway numbers that mass-dialling services flag automatically. Using the Call Log, how many INCOMING calls on ALPHA were identified as Suspected Spam? Tag each one as Evidence with a description.
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Call Log, filter/sort on the spam indicator; tag with the Evidence tag.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Unread traffic can indicate messages that arrived after the device was isolated. How many Instant Messages on ALPHA carry an unread status? Tag them as Leads with a description.
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Instant Messages, filter on status. Tag as Leads.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Push-to-talk applications are a known MERIDIAN tradecraft. What is the username of the Voxer account on ALPHA? Tag it as Evidence and add a description.
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > User Accounts, or search 'Voxer' in All Projects search.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Voice notes are frequently used to pass instructions that avoid text-based collection. What is the file name of the audio file with the LARGEST file size on ALPHA? Tag it as Leads and add a description.
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Audio, Table View, sort descending on Size.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: With known files filtered out, how many .PNG images - minus duplications - are recorded on ALPHA? Capture the totals with the Snipping Tool and add the capture back to the case using File > Add external file.
guideReference: Activity 6.3 Q8, p.468; filters pp.85-86; Activity 1.13, pp.147-150
validationMethod: Images > Table View; apply the non-system (known files) filter, the PNG signature filter and the duplicate rule, then read the totals row.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: The targeting board needs a sense of how much activity this device holds. How many unique Timeline events are on ALPHA?
validationMethod: Application menu > Timeline; read the total event count.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: The commander's window of interest is 1 February 2022 to 1 April 2022. In the Timeline, filter the Timestamp column to that range and clear every Type except Call Logs. How many entries remain?
validationMethod: Timeline > Timestamp column date filter > Apply; Type column > clear all but Call Logs.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Build a watch list named MERIDIAN-NARC containing the keywords Narcotics, Pharmaceuticals, Oxycodone, Oxycontin and Cash, then run it against ALPHA. Where in the Project Tree do the results appear? (Give the full path.)
validationMethod: Tools > WatchList > WatchList Editor to build; Tools > WatchList > Run WatchList to run.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Your partner nation liaison asks how many watch lists and how many entries per list Inseyets.PA supports. What are the limits?
validationMethod: Define up to 50 watch lists with up to 100 entries each.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: You need to share the MERIDIAN-NARC keyword list with a partner agency running its own Inseyets.PA. In what format can watch lists be imported and exported?
validationMethod: Watch lists import and export as CSV files.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: A partner agency supplied a hash set of imagery already associated with the MERIDIAN network. Import the provided CSV hash set, run it against ALPHA, and report how many images matched.
validationMethod: Ctrl+H or Tools > Hash Sets > Hash set manager > Add > CSV File; then Tools > Hash Sets > Run Hash Set. Results at Insights > WatchLists under the Image subcategory.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Where do hash set results appear once the hash set has been run against the case?
options: Insights > WatchLists, under the Image subcategory
acceptedAnswers: Insights > WatchLists, under the Image subcategory
validationMethod: Double-click the hash set entry and review Source file information, MD5, Hash sets and Extraction in Table View.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: ALPHA is passcode protected on a second, still-locked handset recovered at the same site. You generate dictionary files from ALPHA to support that attack. Which three dictionary types does the built-in utility create?
options: A full list of alphanumeric strings starting with the number 1
acceptedAnswers: A full list of alphanumeric strings starting with the number 1
validationMethod: Tools > Generate dictionary files.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: MERIDIAN has previously pushed implants to facilitator handsets. Before scanning ALPHA you must update the malware signatures. Which anti-malware engine does Inseyets.PA use?
validationMethod: Tools > Malware Scanner > Update Signature Database > Update from file.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Your exploitation workstation is air-gapped, so signatures must be updated from a donor file. What is the file name of the definitions file you load?
validationMethod: Air-gapped systems need a donor copy of the BitDefender definitions file from a network-connected Inseyets.PA v10.7.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: Run the malware scan against the ALPHA file systems. How many malware detections are reported?
validationMethod: Tools > Malware Scanner > Scan Malware; watch progress in the Insights window.

sectionTitle: ALPHA Triage: Pattern of Life and Network
prompt: The cell has standardised its tag set for IRON MERIDIAN. Which menu path lets you rename tags, assign hotkeys and create new tags such as Leads?
validationMethod: Tools > Manage Tags; tag sets can be exported for use in other cases or on other computers.

prompt: BRAVO's findings will support a targeting recommendation, so the image must be verified before any of it is briefed. Inseyets.PA can verify the hash obtained during extraction only if the original hash is present in which file?
validationMethod: Extraction Summary > Image Hash > Verify, then View. Open the .ufd in Notepad and read the SHA256 value at the bottom for comparison.

prompt: In Analyzed Data > Images on BRAVO, locate Img_0003.HEIC. What is its byte size?
validationMethod: Search the Images table for Img_0003.HEIC; the guide records byte size 1459886.

prompt: Save Img_0003.HEIC to the desktop, then drag it into Hasher.exe with MD5 selected as the algorithm. What MD5 value does Hasher return, and does it match the MD5 shown by Inseyets.PA? (Give the hash, then Match or No match.)
validationMethod: Hasher.exe is in the Student Folder software directory. Instructor: record the MD5.

prompt: Open Analyzed Data > Messages/Chats > Native Messages on BRAVO and find the thread with the contact Rigoberto (15202229283). How many messages does that thread contain?
validationMethod: The guide records seven messages sent between Jay Walker and Rigoberto.

prompt: To prove the tool decoded that thread correctly you go to the raw database. Using the All Projects search, which database do you open to validate native iOS messages?
validationMethod: All Projects search > type sms.db > Show All > select the sms.db entry.

prompt: Inside sms.db, which table do you open in Database View to compare message bodies against the decoded output?
validationMethod: The guide directs you to the message (80) table.

prompt: You reach the date column of the message table and the value does not look like local time. How are dates and times stored in these databases?
options: In the analyst workstation time zone
validationMethod: Convert with the drop-down suggested timestamp, and remember database times are UTC.

prompt: Complete the validation for all four selected messages in the Rigoberto thread. Record the message body and the converted date/time of the FIRST message in the thread as your flag.
validationMethod: Database View search bar > paste the message body; convert the date column value.

prompt: MERIDIAN imagery is being cross-checked against a partner report, so the EXIF must be validated with a second tool. Save IMG_0041.HEIC from BRAVO and drop it onto ExifTool.exe. Which tab in Inseyets.PA do you open to compare the tool's EXIF output against ExifTool?
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Media > Images; right-click > Save As; ExifTool is command-line based - drag the file onto ExifTool.exe rather than launching it.

prompt: You open the Calendar entry 'flyhome' in the CalendarItem table and the start_date is a large integer. Seconds are counted from which epoch?
validationMethod: MAC Absolute Time (CF Absolute Time) is based on 1 January 2001 00:00:00 UTC and is used by iOS since iOS 5.

prompt: Install and launch DCode, paste the start_date value, and set the time zone to UTC-7:00 Arizona. What Apple Absolute Time (UTC) value does DCode return, and does it match the decoded start date in Analyzed Data > Calendar > Work?
validationMethod: DCode is in the Student Folder software directory. Instructor: record the decoded value.

prompt: Three copies of IMG_0006 exist on BRAVO. To establish which one carries the true capture location you go to Photos.sqlite. Which TABLE holds ZLATITUDE and ZLONGITUDE - the accurate location of the original image when it was taken?
validationMethod: The primary key is the photo number. Also explore ZASSET and ZCLOUDMASTERMEDIAMETADATA (ZDATA column, BPList serialized data).

prompt: Compare IMG_0006.heic (DCIM), IMG_0006.heic (SMS) and 005.jpg on MD5 hash, date/time and location. Which is the ORIGINAL, which is the THUMBNAIL, and which has been ALTERED? (Answer in that order.)
validationMethod: Use Hasher for the MD5s, ExifTool for the EXIF, and Photos.sqlite for the true location.

prompt: The device is available, powered on, and the passcode is known. Your section chief asks whether you can hand scroll it to confirm a finding. What is the governing rule?
options: Hand scroll first so you know what to look for during extraction
All extractions must be performed prior to hand scrolling, and the device placed in a no-network state
Hand scrolling is prohibited once a device is in evidence
Hand scrolling replaces the need for third-party validation
acceptedAnswers: All extractions must be performed prior to hand scrolling, and the device placed in a no-network state
validationMethod: Hand scrolling can change data on the device; disable cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and NFC, and photograph and document any new findings.

prompt: CHARLIE arrived as an iTunes backup rather than a UFED extraction, so it must be opened through Open (Advanced). During ingest you are prompted for the backup password. What is it?
validationMethod: +Add Evidence > Common Source > Backup > iTunes backup > Select Folder (select the entire folder, do not open it).

prompt: Open (Advanced) is the right tool for CHARLIE. Which statement about it is correct?
options: It can only open files produced by a UFED unit
If a .ufd file is corrupt or missing, Open (Advanced) can create a new one
It cannot process iTunes or iCloud backups
It requires the device to be physically connected
acceptedAnswers: If a .ufd file is corrupt or missing, Open (Advanced) can create a new one
validationMethod: Open (Advanced) handles .bin, .dd, .img, iTunes/iCloud backups, JTAG, ISP and chip-off extractions.

prompt: AirDrop activity is a known MERIDIAN method for moving files without network logging. What is the AirDrop ID for CHARLIE?
validationMethod: Device Info / Extraction Summary. Instructor: record the observed value.

prompt: The equipment annex of your report needs the exact hardware. What is the model number of CHARLIE?
validationMethod: Device Info. Instructor: record the observed value.

prompt: How long does CHARLIE retain messages before automatic deletion? (Message retention duration.)
validationMethod: Device Info. This drives how far back message content can be expected to exist.

prompt: Your timeline must be presented in the target's local time. What time zone is set on CHARLIE?
guideReference: Activity 6.4 Q4, p.472; Project Settings p.59
validationMethod: Device Info; then confirm your project time zone setting matches your reporting standard.

prompt: Was the iTunes backup on CHARLIE set to be encrypted?
validationMethod: Device Info / backup settings. Instructor: confirm and key the correct option.

prompt: Communications tradecraft assessment: list FIVE messaging applications used on CHARLIE.
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Installed Applications, or the Top 5 messaging apps widget.

prompt: Were there any pictures sent by MMS or iMessage on CHARLIE?
validationMethod: Messages > filter on attachments. Instructor: confirm and key the correct option.

prompt: Cloud accounts extend collection beyond the handset. Was an iCloud account found on CHARLIE?
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > User Accounts. Instructor: confirm and key the correct option.

prompt: Network analysis: who were the TOP FIVE messaging parties on CHARLIE?
validationMethod: Use the Top 5 messaging parties widget.

prompt: Which database on CHARLIE contains the most records (rows)?
validationMethod: Analyzed Data > Data Files > Databases; sort on record count.

prompt: Using the advanced filter within Timeline on CHARLIE, how many searched items and contacts are there in total?
validationMethod: Timeline > Type column filter; select only Searched Items and Contacts and read the total.

prompt: Movement assessment: was CHARLIE ever in Dhaka, Bangladesh?
validationMethod: Locations view plus offline maps. Instructor: confirm and key the correct option.

prompt: Imagery volume on CHARLIE is too large to review by hand, so you run the automated classifier. Give the full menu path used to run media classification after a case has already been ingested.
validationMethod: Choose the media type (Image and Video, Image, or Video) and the categories relevant to the mission.

prompt: Where do you go to review the results of media classification once processing completes? (Give the full path.)
validationMethod: You can also expand the Images and Videos categories under Analyzed Data.

prompt: Run media classification on CHARLIE with all categories selected. How many items are classified under the Substance category?
validationMethod: Insights > Media Classification > Substance. Note the number shown under the category.

prompt: Open the Drugs subcategory on CHARLIE and review the thumbnails. Identify at least two FALSE POSITIVES and explain, in one or two sentences each, why the classifier flagged them and why you are excluding them from the intelligence picture.
validationMethod: Rubric: names two specific items, gives a plausible classifier rationale, and states the exclusion decision. The guide warns classifications must be reviewed carefully for false positives.

prompt: The geospatial cell wants CHARLIE's location data. In the Locations view, into which categories is location data organised?
validationMethod: Double-click a category to open it in Table View and filter by Source.

prompt: Your workstation is air-gapped, so the map tiles will not load from the internet. What menu path installs the offline maps package?
acceptedAnswers: Tools > Offline maps > Install offline maps package
validationMethod: Map packs download from Community.Cellebrite.com > Products and Licensing > Physical Analyzer.

prompt: In the Locations > Media table on CHARLIE, select several entries, right-click and choose Retrieve Address. Export the selected locations as a KML file. What EXPORT option do you choose, and what third-party application does the guide have you load the file into for comparison?
validationMethod: Export > KML (locations); load the .KML into Google Earth and compare against Inseyets.PA.

prompt: You run AppGenie against CHARLIE's unsupported regional applications and it surfaces several new chat threads. How must those results be treated in your reporting?
options: As confirmed intelligence, since AppGenie uses AI
As initial indicators only; findings are not fully validated and require verification
As confirmed only if the application is on the supported list
acceptedAnswers: As initial indicators only; findings are not fully validated and require verification
validationMethod: Tools > AppGenie, or Analyzed Data > Application > Installed Applications > Insights.

prompt: Run AppGenie against CHARLIE. Name ONE application from which AppGenie parsed artifacts that were not present in the standard decoded output, and state what artifact type it recovered (contacts, user accounts, or chats).
validationMethod: Instructor: run AppGenie once against the classroom image and record acceptable answers.

prompt: DELTA's imagery is the crux of the collection requirement, but the tool's decoded view does not carry the file paths the targeting cell needs. Open Photos.sqlite and launch the wizard. Give the two menu routes that open the SQLite Wizard.
acceptedAnswers: Tools > SQLite Wizard; or open the Table view for the database and select the SQLite Wizard icon
validationMethod: You can also choose Export to CSV or Open in DB Viewer from the same place.

prompt: In the SQLite Wizard launch screen, 'Include deleted rows' is NOT selected by default. Why?
options: It is not supported for Apple databases
To prevent the increased chance of false positives
Because deleted rows are covered by data carving instead
Because it requires a physical extraction
acceptedAnswers: To prevent the increased chance of false positives
validationMethod: Select it deliberately when recovery of deleted rows is worth the false-positive risk.

prompt: The Query Builder workspace is divided into four areas. Name them.
validationMethod: Only tables are shown in the Table View window - indexes, triggers and views do not appear.

prompt: Drag ZCLOUDMASTER into the Work area and select ZORIGINALFILENAME, ZCREATIONDATE and ZIMPORTDATE. According to the database schema (sqlite_master), what is the PRIMARY KEY of the ZCLOUDMASTER table?
validationMethod: Read the schema in sqlite_master before building the join.

prompt: You drag the ZCLOUDMASTER primary key onto the matching ZCLOUDRESOURCE foreign key and a black line appears. Which join type does SQLite Wizard apply by default?
validationMethod: Double-click the black line to open Link Properties and change the join type.

prompt: Your preview is returning only a handful of rows and you know the table is larger. What is the DEFAULT value of the Max results field that you must increase?
validationMethod: Cellebrite recommends setting Max results to the next value above the total record count.

prompt: Select ZFILESIZE and ZFILEPATH from ZCLOUDRESOURCE, map the query using the generic model, and drop a Timestamp field type onto ZCREATIONDATE and ZIMPORTDATE. After you select Run, in which Analyzed Data location do the new records appear? (Give the full path.)
validationMethod: The new entries can then be reviewed, tagged and added to the report.

prompt: After running your Photos.sqlite query, how many records are shown in the New records column of the SQLite Query Manager?
validationMethod: Instructor: run the query once against the classroom image and record the count.

prompt: A MERIDIAN chat application is unsupported. One table holds the message body in ZBODY with an author reference in ZUSER; a second table holds Z_PK and ZUSERNAME. Write the chain of attributes that must be linked to produce a readable table of messages with author names.
validationMethod: Links must exist between these attributes to map the artifacts into a readable table.

prompt: While reviewing a MERIDIAN chat table you notice the _id values run 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9. What does the guide say this indicates, and what does it let you report?
options: A database error; the table should be re-parsed
Primary key gaps indicating possible deleted records, supporting an estimate of the amount of deleted content
Normal SQLite behaviour with no analytic value
acceptedAnswers: Primary key gaps indicating possible deleted records, supporting an estimate of the amount of deleted content
validationMethod: Document primary key gaps as indicators of possible data destruction and consider unallocated space review and database carving.

prompt: MERIDIAN's application stores an image blob and a set of coordinates in the same table. Which SQLite storage classes does the guide list?
validationMethod: Real stores an 8-byte floating point number and can hold coordinates; BLOB stores images and documents.

prompt: Export the generic model table as an Excel spreadsheet named PhotosDatabaseSpreadsheet, rename the generic column headers to their database descriptors, then bring the spreadsheet back into the case so it can be included in the report. Which menu path adds it back?
validationMethod: In the Additional Files window set File Name, Category and Notes, then Add to Project.

prompt: Validation statement. Compare your SQLite Wizard output against the decoded Analyzed Data view for the same records. State whether the tool output matches the raw database, describe any discrepancy, and state the validation method you used. This statement will be lifted directly into the intelligence report.
guideReference: Lesson 4.1, p.350; Mini-mission 4.2, pp.390-392; Mini-mission 5.4, pp.422-423
validationMethod: Rubric: states match/no-match, names the second method used, and documents any discrepancy as resolved or unresolved.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: ECHO is a legacy feature phone recovered from a weapons cache. Its SMS records are not fully decoded, so you must benchmark the message structure by hand in the MCU [6MB] memory image. What ASCII marker sits between each SMS message on this device?
validationMethod: File Systems > Memory Images > MCU [6MB]; the marker is visible in the ASCII view.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: You want to find every one of those markers. What HEX value do you enter in Find > Bytes > Hex to search for that ASCII string?
validationMethod: Highlight the marker in hex, right-click Copy, then Find > Bytes > Hex and paste.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Counting from the end of that marker, how many bytes forward does the SMS message body begin?
validationMethod: Benchmarking result for this device: the SMS body starts 38 bytes after the marker.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: What is the maximum size, in bytes, of the SMS body on this device?
validationMethod: 140 bytes is the total space allotted for the body of an SMS message on this device.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: While highlighting the body you hit a long run of a repeating byte. What hex value is used as padding, which you should NOT include in your selection?
validationMethod: Highlight only non-null values; 0xFF is padding.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: The party identifier for one recovered message reads 0B917106696041F8. Decode it to a telephone number in international format.
validationMethod: Stored in nibble-reverse format with the trailing F removed as a null value.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: In that same value, what do the leading bytes 0B and 91 tell you?
options: 0B = 11 digits in the number; 91 = international format
acceptedAnswers: 0B = 11 digits in the number; 91 = international format
validationMethod: Apply the same logic to any other party identifier you recover.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Decode the party identifier 0B917106992681F5 using the same method.
validationMethod: Nibble reverse, drop the trailing F.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: You have highlighted the non-null bytes of a recovered SMS body. Give the exact path in the Values view that decodes it to readable text.
validationMethod: Then right-click the highlighted bytes > Add tags and label the hex tag, e.g. Recovered SMS Body.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Give the exact path in the Values view that decodes the recovered message's timestamp.
acceptedAnswers: Date & Time > Generic > PDU SMS time
validationMethod: The SMSC number is decoded at Numbers > SMS > SMSC Number.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Recover ONE SMS message from unallocated space on ECHO that the automated decoding did not surface. Report the decoded body text, the decoded party number, and the PDU timestamp. Tag the hex range as Recovered SMS Body.
validationMethod: Instructor: work one message through in advance and record an acceptable answer set. Multiple correct answers exist; accept any correctly decoded message.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Human intelligence indicates a message referencing 'Deputyjorge'. You run Find > Strings > ASCII for that term against the MCU image and get no result. What do you do next and why?
options: Re-run automated decoding; the search index is stale
Search again using 7 Bit, because SMS content is stored in a 7-bit encoded state in flash memory
Carve the unallocated space for JPEGs instead
Conclude the message was never on the device
acceptedAnswers: Search again using 7 Bit, because SMS content is stored in a 7-bit encoded state in flash memory
validationMethod: Find > Strings > 7 Bit > Term: Deputyjorge.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: The decoded Deputyjorge message in the Instant Messages content area carries what date and time?
validationMethod: Content area > Instant Messages > search Deputyjorge.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Imagery was deleted from ECHO before capture. Give the menu path that runs automated image carving.
acceptedAnswers: Tools > Get more data (Carving) > Carve Images
validationMethod: Select Scan Type (Quick scan) and Carve From (Unallocated space).

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Your section chief asks why you cannot carve images from BRAVO's advanced logical extraction. What is the correct answer?
options: Carving requires the device to be present
Image carving is only available for physical extractions
Carving requires the Enrichment Engine licence
acceptedAnswers: Image carving is only available for physical extractions
validationMethod: Carving retrieves data from unallocated space and rebuilds images; it is not run automatically because of processing cost.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: You need the maximum number of recoverable JPEGs and you accept a higher rate of non-viewable output. Which scan type do you choose?
validationMethod: Quick scan finds the fewest images fastest; Full scan adds JPEG headers to matching compression patterns; Full scan without filter removes the false-positive filter.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Where do carved image results appear once carving completes? (Give the section of Analyzed Data.)
validationMethod: The number beside the image carving results is the total number of image files carved.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: You now carve by hand. What HEX value do you search for in Find > Bytes > Hex to locate image file markers, and what does it translate to in ASCII?
validationMethod: The Offset column gives the location of each hit; the Source column links to the value in memory; the More column shows associated file paths and names.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Run the JFIF byte search against the ECHO MCU image. How many hits are returned?
validationMethod: Instructor: run the search once and record the hit count.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: FOXTROT was taken from a detainee who will not give his name. The lead wants any email address in the memory image. Navigate to File Systems > Memory Images > Flex and open Find > RegEx (GREP). Write the regular expression the guide provides for locating email addresses.
validationMethod: Ensure there are no spaces in the expression. Select Add to save it to the library, then Save it to disk for reuse.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Run that expression against FOXTROT. Report every unique email address recovered, and save the expression to the library with the description Email Search.
guideReference: Activity 3.7 regex activity, pp.277-279; Mini-mission 3.6, pp.280-281
validationMethod: Instructor: run the expression once and record the address list.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: You want the last places FOXTROT's user searched for or visited. You run Tools > Get More Data (Carving) > Carve locations with Carve Most Visited Sites selected. What is the limit of that option?
options: All sites within a 5 km radius
Sites visited in the last 24 hours
validationMethod: Custom Radius lets you position a pin on a map and set a radius.

sectionTitle: ECHO and FOXTROT: Legacy Handsets and Hex-Level Recovery
prompt: Your geospatial product will drive a physical action, so it must be defensible. Select one location finding from FOXTROT or CHARLIE, state the source type (GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower, notification or media EXIF), assign a confidence level of confirmed, probable or possible, and justify it. Name one external source you would use to validate it.
validationMethod: Rubric: correct source type, defensible confidence level, and a named external source such as call detail records or operational intelligence. Credit answers that note GPS is high precision while Wi-Fi and cell tower are lower precision, or that map data may include searched-but-never-visited locations, or that social media tags can differ from EXIF.

prompt: GOLF is a binary dump from a handset Inseyets.PA does not recognise. Give the menu path that opens the tool used to review and build plug-in chains.
validationMethod: Select All Chains to review existing chains; My Chains to build your own.

prompt: You load the GOLF binary dump using a randomly selected Android chain. What result does the guide tell you to expect?
options: A complete decode with minor errors
Automatic substitution of the correct chain
validationMethod: The wrong chain produces effectively nothing; delete the case and try again with the correct chain.

prompt: Rebuild the case, select Switch Chain, and search for the correct chain for this MCU binary dump. What is the exact name of the chain that successfully decodes it?
validationMethod: +Add Evidence > Open Advanced > Blank Project > Switch Chain > All Chains > search.

prompt: In what languages are Inseyets.PA plug-ins written?
validationMethod: A chain is a series of plug-ins configured to run in a set order.

prompt: Before running a plug-in a partner agency sent you, you double-click it in the Add/Remove Plug-ins window. What does the Plug-in Status dialog tell you, and what does it mean?
options: Version number; whether an update is available
Signed or unsigned; a signed plug-in was approved and signed by Cellebrite
Pass or fail; whether it ran successfully last time
Chain membership; which chains use it
acceptedAnswers: Signed or unsigned; a signed plug-in was approved and signed by Cellebrite
validationMethod: Built-in Cellebrite plug-ins are proprietary and cannot be edited or uninstalled.

prompt: Document your custom chain for team reuse: name the chain with a mission-appropriate name, list the plug-ins or source chains you used, state why this device required a custom chain, and quantify the improvement over the default chain output.
validationMethod: Rubric: chain saved under a mission-appropriate name, composition documented, justification given, and results compared against the default chain output.

prompt: With the correct chain applied, report ONE item of intelligence value recovered from GOLF that was not available under the default chain. State the data type and the value.
validationMethod: Instructor: run both chains in advance and record acceptable answers.

prompt: The partner agency requires password protection on everything it receives. Which report formats support password protection?
validationMethod: Password protection is NOT available for HTML or XML.

prompt: UFDR protection encrypts the report file to protect the raw extracted data it contains. What encryption standard is used?
validationMethod: UFDR reports are encrypted using AES encryption with CBC.

prompt: A supported unit has no Inseyets.PA licence but needs to work through the findings themselves. What do you distribute with the report?
options: Cellebrite Reader, a free portable application with most analytical features removed
acceptedAnswers: Cellebrite Reader, a free portable application with most analytical features removed
validationMethod: Include Reader is a UFDR-only option; the Reader executable is placed in the report output folder. It can be encrypted and password protected.

prompt: The analytical cell wants to ingest your product into an advanced link-analysis tool. Which Cellebrite analytic tool does the guide name as the destination for UFDR and XML reports?
validationMethod: XML assists with Unicode-based languages and can be imported by other analysis tools.

prompt: The field team needs something in the next ten minutes covering device attributes and account identifiers only. Which Inseyets.PA report type meets that requirement?
validationMethod: It gives a quick high-level summary of device and account information for analysts, operators and commanders.

prompt: Your commander asks for the difference between the report Inseyets.PA generates and the product your cell writes. Which statement is correct?
options: They are the same product under different names

An exploitation report documents artifacts recovered during extraction but does not provide full operational context or chronology; an intelligence report is an analyst narrative with a full timeline, authority, tools used and conclusions
An intelligence report is generated automatically from tagged items
An exploitation report must always be classified higher than an intelligence report
acceptedAnswers: An exploitation report documents artifacts recovered during extraction but does not provide full operational context or chronology; an intelligence report is an analyst narrative with a full timeline, authority, tools used and conclusions
validationMethod: Tool-generated reports may be included as attachments to the intelligence report.

prompt: Your intelligence report must document how each device was received and handled. Which device-identification questions does the guide require you to answer?
options: What is the make and model of the device?
What was the state of the device (powered on vs off)?
What steps were taken to isolate the device from the network?
What is the retail value of the device?
acceptedAnswers: What is the make and model of the device?
What was the state of the device (powered on vs off)?
What steps were taken to isolate the device from the network?
validationMethod: Also: where the device originated, distinguishing characteristics, chain of custody or handling record, and associated or supporting devices.

prompt: Generate a Tags Only report in PDF format covering your tagged findings across all cases. How many tagged items are included in the report?
validationMethod: Depends on the student's own tagging. Score against the student's tag count as displayed in Manage Tags / the generated report, not against a fixed number.

prompt: Generate a UFDR report including all default data types, file types and preferences categories, and apply protection appropriate for partner release. State the protection you applied and the file name of the report you produced.
guideReference: Activity 6.1, p.461; Lesson 6.1, p.433; Mini-mission 6.2, pp.461-463
validationMethod: Accept any answer that names UFDR AES protection and/or password protection plus the student's actual file name.

prompt: Storage guidance for the completed products: which practice does the guide direct?
options: Store products on the analysis workstation's local drive only
Archive reports on network storage or another solution using a RAID configuration, and strongly consider encrypting reports stored on portable drives if authorised
Email products to all supported units immediately
Delete products once the brief is complete
acceptedAnswers: Archive reports on network storage or another solution using a RAID configuration, and strongly consider encrypting reports stored on portable drives if authorised
validationMethod: Storing on a remote drive prevents data loss and lets other operators produce the intelligence briefing.

prompt: Commander's Priority Intelligence Requirement. In no more than 300 words, answer PIR 1: Who within the MERIDIAN network directs the movement of controlled components, and through what communications means? Support every assertion with the specific device, artifact and location in Inseyets.PA where you found it, and state the validation method used for each of your three strongest findings.
validationMethod: Rubric (40 pts): names a directing individual with cross-device support (10); identifies the communications means with the artifact cited (10); cites device, artifact and Inseyets.PA location for each assertion (10); states a second-tool or raw-database validation method for three findings (10). Deduct for speculation unsupported by a cited artifact - reporting must remain objective and unbiased.
